note: The most physical book in the Studios: a lonely inn on a cove, Bristol docks, a ship at sea, an island. Every gun comes twice — near (sharp, dry, loud) and far (muffled, late, long echo) — and most of the shooting is far. Part One is the Admiral Benbow; Part Two the Bristol docks, the Spy-glass and the Hispaniola — the surf below the cliff, the parlour fire, the stick on the frozen road, the riders on the hill. Shared sounds are borrowed from Dracula by URL. THE CREW’S DEATH MOTIF: each time one of the ship’s company dies — honest man or pirate — the cellos and basses play a slow “yo… ho”, a short D and a long low A, the shape of the crew’s chant with the life gone out of it — and gulls crying over it, one near as the “ho” sounds, one answering further off.

cove.note: surf on the rocks below the cliff, the wind off the sea

inn.note: the parlour fire at the Admiral Benbow

docks.note: Bristol: water slapping the wharf piles, moored boats working, gulls

deck.note: the Hispaniola: the hull working, wind in the rigging, canvas, a block creaking

tavern.note: the Spy-glass: a bright little tavern, a fire in the grate

island.note: the island in a stagnant heat: insects shrilling in the woods, the surf booming far off, shore birds

stockade.note: the log-house on its knoll: the island’s heat and insects around it

coracle.note: the theme’s coda water: lapping close against a little hull, the boat creaking, the surf far off
